ddl:
CREATE TABLE User (
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Role VARCHAR(255),
    User_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Username VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Building (
    Building_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Description VARCHAR(255),
    Dormitory_Supervisor_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Location VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Type VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (Dormitory_Supervisor_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Announcement (
    Administrator_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Announcement_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Content VARCHAR(255),
    Release_Time DATETIME,
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (Administrator_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Dormitory (
    Building_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Dormitory_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Facilities VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Number_of_Beds INTEGER,
    Type VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (Building_ID) REFERENCES Building(Building_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Student (
    Class VARCHAR(255),
    Dormitory_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Gender VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Student_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    FOREIGN KEY (Dormitory_ID) REFERENCES Dormitory(Dormitory_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Maintenance_Record (
    Completion_Time DATETIME,
    Dormitory_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Fault_Description VARCHAR(255),
    Maintenance_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Maintenance_Staff_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Maintenance_Status VARCHAR(255),
    Report_Time DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (Dormitory_ID) REFERENCES Dormitory(Dormitory_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maintenance_Staff_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Application (
    Application_Content VARCHAR(255),
    Application_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Application_Time DATETIME,
    Application_Type VARCHAR(255),
    Processing_Opinion VARCHAR(255),
    Processing_Status VARCHAR(255),
    Student_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Student_ID) REFERENCES Student(Student_ID)
);

The student dormitory management system business requirement description:
A student dormitory management system includes functions such as user management, building management, dormitory management, and student management. The system has users with different roles, such as administrators, dormitory managers, students, and maintenance staff. Each user has a unique ID, username, and password. Building information includes building ID, name, type, location, description, and the responsible dormitory manager. Dormitory information includes dormitory ID, name, type, number of beds, belonging building, supporting facilities, and the responsible dormitory manager. Student information includes student ID, name, gender, belonging dormitory, class, etc. Students can submit various applications (bed change, repair, absence registration, check-out application, etc.). The system records application ID, application type, applicant student ID, application content, application time, application status, and administrator's processing opinion. Administrators can process these applications, review and approve or reject them. Dormitory managers can handle students' leave and repair applications, and manage absence registration. Maintenance staff can handle repair applications and record maintenance information. Maintenance records include maintenance record ID, dormitory ID, fault description, repair time, maintenance staff ID, maintenance situation, and completion time. The system also includes announcement management for administrators to publish and manage announcement information. Announcement information includes announcement ID, announcement title, announcement content, release time, and the ID of the administrator who released the announcement.

This database schema, named rschema_0425, is used to store information about a university dormitory and its residents. It consists of seven tables: User, Building, Announcement, Dormitory, Student, Maintenance_Record, and Application.
The User table contains information about the users of the system, including their passwords, roles, and usernames. The Role column specifies whether the user is an administrator, a dormitory supervisor, or a student. The User_ID column is the primary key for the table.
The Building table contains information about the dormitories, including their names, descriptions, locations, and types. The Building_ID column is the primary key for the table, and the Dormitory_Supervisor_ID column references the User table to specify the dormitory supervisor.
The Announcement table contains information about announcements made by the dormitory supervisor, including the title, content, and release time. The Administrator_ID column references the User table to specify the announcement author, and the Announcement_ID column is the primary key for the table.
The Dormitory table contains information about the dormitories, including their names, numbers of beds, and facilities. The Dormitory_ID column is the primary key for the table, and the Building_ID column references the Building table to specify the dormitory's building.
The Student table contains information about the students who live in the dormitories, including their names, genders, and classes. The Student_ID column is the primary key for the table, and the Dormitory_ID column references the Dormitory table to specify the student's dormitory.
The Maintenance_Record table contains information about maintenance requests made by students or dormitory supervisors, including the fault description, report time, completion time, and maintenance status. The Maintenance_ID column is the primary key for the table, and the Dormitory_ID column references the Dormitory table to specify the maintenance request's dormitory.
The Application table contains information about applications made by students, including the application type, content, application time, processing status, and processing opinion. The Application_ID column is the primary key for the table, and the Student_ID column references the Student table to specify the application's student.
In summary, this schema stores information about a university dormitory and its residents, including users, buildings, announcements, dormitories, students, maintenance requests, and applications. The schema enforces domain integrity by specifying data types for each column and ensuring that certain columns cannot be null. It also enforces entity integrity by specifying primary keys and foreign keys, and ensures referential integrity by specifying update and delete rules for foreign keys.
